Anthem: a planned community outside any city

Anthem sits along Interstate 17 at the north edge of the Valley, an unincorporated master-planned community in Maricopa County rather than a town with its own council. That has two practical effects for a pool owner. Water does not come from a city department, it comes from EPCOR, a private water utility that publishes a separate water quality report for its Anthem system. And city codes that cover neighbors to the south do not apply here, so the rules for a permit, a barrier or a drain are county rules, often alongside homeowners association rules.

Where the homes on a street went up around the same time, their pools tend to reach the same milestones together: a first pump replacement, a first heater problem, a first plaster that has gone rough. When one neighbor starts asking about pool resurfacing or equipment repair, others on the street are often not far behind.

Pool service Anthem AZ homeowners call about

Hard water drives a lot of Anthem calls. White crust at the waterline points to pool tile cleaning, a heater that scales up and stops heating points to pool heater repair, and filters clogged with scale and fine desert dust call for filter cleaning. Routine weekly cleaning and maintenance is where a pool company catches calcium before it sets.

Where Anthem's water comes from

EPCOR's report for the Anthem system names Colorado River water carried by the Central Arizona Project (CAP) as its main source. That water comes from the CAP canal and is treated at the Anthem Water Treatment Plant, which the utility describes as a microfiltration plant. The report adds that the supply contains both surface water and groundwater, which is why hardness and taste can change with the seasons.

Microfiltration is a very fine filter. It strains out particles and microbes, but it does not take out dissolved calcium and magnesium, so the treated water stays hard. And because the blend can shift between sources, the water you fill with in one season may not test the same as the water you fill with in another.

Hardness and minerals in EPCOR's 2024 Anthem water quality report
EPCOR Anthem reportHardnessCalciumOther readings
2024 reportAbout 18 grains per gallon80 ppmMagnesium 29 ppm, total dissolved solids 640 mg/L, pH 8.2

For scale, 18 grains per gallon works out to roughly 300 milligrams per liter of hardness. Total dissolved solids (TDS) is everything dissolved in the water, minerals and salts together. The U.S. EPA's secondary, non-enforceable guideline for TDS in drinking water is 500 milligrams per liter, so Anthem's fill water starts above that mark before a single gallon evaporates from the pool.

What very hard fill water does to a pool

Evaporation takes water and leaves minerals behind. Each top off with 18 grain water adds more. These are the places it shows up first.

The waterline tile

Calcium deposits form a white or gray band where the water meets the tile. Caught early it comes off with care. Left for years it hardens, and removing it becomes a job for a professional.

Heaters and salt cells

Heat pulls calcium out of the water, so scale collects inside heater exchangers and on salt cell plates. A scaled heater runs hot and heats poorly, and a scaled cell makes less chlorine.

Plaster and pebble finishes

Water that is out of balance either leaves scale on the surface or slowly etches it. A careful technician tests calcium, pH, alkalinity and stabilizer together and adjusts toward balance.

Looking after an Anthem pool between visits

You do not need to be a chemist. A few safe habits help a pool company keep hard water in check:

  • Top off before it drops far. Keep the water about halfway up the skimmer opening so the pump does not draw air.
  • Watch the waterline. Mention new white crust right away. Fresh deposits are easier to remove than old ones.
  • Note the filter gauge. A pressure reading that keeps climbing means the filter is loading up with dust and scale.
  • Test with a home kit. Strips or a drop kit give you chlorine and pH readings to share. Leave adjustments with strong chemicals to the pool company.
  • Check the heater area. If you smell gas near a gas pool heater, leave the area, do not touch switches or the heater, and from a safe distance phone 911 or the emergency number for your gas provider.

Store chemicals safely. Never mix pool chemicals with each other. Keep them apart, dry, shaded and out of children's reach, follow the label, and leave acid work to a professional. And never leave a child alone near the pool, even for a moment.

Questions to ask an Anthem pool company

  • Do you test calcium hardness and TDS, and how often? In Anthem water these matter as much as chlorine.
  • What is your Arizona ROC license number? Ask before repairs, equipment, resurfacing or leak work, then check it on the ROC search.
  • How do you handle scale on the tile and in the heater? Ask what method they use and what it costs before work starts.
  • If you drain the pool, where does the water go? Ask them to name the county or HOA rule they follow.

Common questions

Where does Anthem, AZ get its water?

From EPCOR, a private water utility, not a city. EPCOR's water quality report for Anthem names Colorado River water delivered by the Central Arizona Project, piped from the CAP canal and treated at the Anthem Water Treatment Plant, and it says the supply contains both surface water and groundwater, so hardness and taste can vary with the seasons.

How hard is the water in Anthem?

EPCOR's 2024 Anthem report puts hardness at about 18 grains per gallon, with calcium at 80 parts per million and total dissolved solids at 640 milligrams per liter. That is very hard water, and a pool filled and topped off with it builds calcium quickly.

Do I need to drain my Anthem pool because of the hard water?

Not on a schedule. Draining lowers calcium and dissolved solids for a while, but the refill water is hard too, and an empty pool in Arizona sun has its own risks. Have the pool company test the water and explain what the numbers say before anyone drains. The pool draining guide covers the tradeoffs.

Is there pool service in Anthem at night or on weekends?

The line is staffed by an automated assistant around the clock and transfers you to an independent pool company that works in Anthem. Whether that company can come out at night or on a weekend, and what it charges for that, is up to the company, so ask when you are connected.

Does Anthem follow City of Phoenix pool rules?

Generally no. Anthem is an unincorporated community in Maricopa County, so City of Phoenix codes do not cover it, and its water is not City of Phoenix water. Ask the pool company which county rules apply to a drain, a new barrier or equipment work, and check any homeowners association rules too.
